knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Slope of a Normal Line to a Curve at a Point

question.:question/problem:
Find the slope $m'$ of the normal line to the curve

$$
y=(x-3)(x^{2}+x)
$$

at the point $\left(1,-4\right)$. Give an exact answer.

$m'=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=(x-3)(x^{2}+x)$. Expand and combine like terms before differentiating.

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=x^{3}+x^{2}-3x^{2}-3x\\
&=x^{3}-2x^{2}-3x
\end{aligned}
$$

Apply the power rule:

$$
f'(x)=3x^{2}-4x-3
$$

The tangent slope at $\left(1,-4\right)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
m=f'(1)&=3\left(1\right)^{2}-4\left(1\right)-3\\
&=3-4-3\\
&=-4
\end{aligned}
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so take the negative reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}
m'&=-\frac{1}{m}\\
&=-\frac{1}{\left(-4\right)}\\
&=\frac{1}{4}
\end{aligned}
$$
